variation.what_moved: One email of twenty-four, 016-slatemoor-remit-to-update. In passes 1 and 2 it came back benign. In pass 3 the closing answer hit the 512 token ceiling part way through a nineteen item indicator list, so the JSON never closed, no verdict was read, and four of the six note lines read 'not answered'. That row's escalate flag then went to yes on the low confidence rule, which is why escalation agreement reads 13 in pass 3 and 12 in the other two. The agreement went up because an email failed, not because the agent judged better.

variation.what_a_student_will_see: The verdict, the escalate flag, the stop reason and the two tool calls on email 018 were the same in all three passes. The confidence, the recommended action and the wording of the summary were not. Say the first group on camera. Do not promise the second.

headline: The agent called a phishing message benign in all three runs, and wrote a summary telling the person who reported it that nothing is wrong. The escalate line on that same note still reads yes, because the student's own fact check set it, not the model. Over twenty-four emails the agent was right sixteen times, with zero false positives and eight false negatives: every error it made was the expensive kind.
